argument:
1. Integration and provenance.
The three supplied drafts and all six of their declared source dependencies were read in full. Their byte SHA-256 values were computed locally and matched _snapshot.json. The drafts prove essentially the same theorem: neither purported review draft supplies an independent review of an identified unchanged integration. Their overlapping arguments are deduplicated below. The explicit recipe-isometry verification in draft 3e5b… is retained. No numerical catalogue result, prior review vote, SELF lemma, M5 existence theorem, or stage-1 stabilization result is a mathematical premise. The M5 sources supply the admissible input interface; its mathematical conventions are checked directly. The C105 sources distinguish revoked certificates from their reported replacements and warn that module shears need not preserve weight; neither set of finite distance claims is invoked here.

2. Physical spaces and full multiplicities.
Put M=x^N+1 and S=GF(2)[x]/(M), representing each physical block by its N coefficients. Row combinations of H_X are L(h)=(ah,bh), h∈S. Indeed row i is (x^ia,x^ib). Since Bᵀ_{i,j}=b_{i-j}, the H_Z syndrome of (u,v) is the coefficient vector of bu+av. Thus B_X=im L and C_X={(u,v):bu+av=0}. Characteristic two and commutativity imply B_X⊆C_X.
An ordinary polynomial Bézout identity F=pa+qb+rM shows that ah=bh=0 in S implies Fh=0. The converse follows because F divides a and b. Write M=FK. For the degree-less-than-N representative H of h, M|FH iff K|H, by cancellation in GF(2)[x]. Such representatives are exactly Kt with deg t<f, including only zero when f=0. Consequently ker L has 2^f elements, dim B_X=N−f, and every boundary has exactly 2^f preimages. This argument never replaces a polynomial by its radical and remains valid when N is even.
Define the coordinate permutation J by J(u,v)_i=(v_{−i},u_{−i}), with indices modulo N. It preserves weight and dot products and is an involution. It sends row i of H_X to row −i of H_Z, so B_Z=row(H_Z)=JB_X and C_X=B_Z^⊥ has dimension N+f. Also JC_X=B_X^⊥=C_Z and JB_X=B_Z. Therefore J bijects the two types of nonboundary cycles, and the logical dimension is 2f.

3. Transfer construction and exact cyclic indexing.
Pad a,b through degree R. A memory state m=(m_1,…,m_R) records the preceding R input bits, most recent first. An edge labeled t∈{0,1} goes to σ(m,t)=(t,m_1,…,m_{R−1}) and outputs the bits
α=a_0t+Σ_{j=1}^R a_jm_j,  β=b_0t+Σ_{j=1}^R b_jm_j,
where these sums are in GF(2). Set e=α+β as an ordinary integer. When R=0 there is one empty state and two distinct labeled loops.
Every indexed cyclic input h_0,…,h_{N−1} determines a closed length-N walk by m_{i,j}=h_{i−j}, with indices modulo N. Conversely, periodically extend any closed labeled walk. Applying the shift rule backward j times gives m_{i,j}=h_{i−j}, so its appended bits determine all states uniquely. These constructions are inverse, including empty memory. Outputs at layer i are exactly (ah)_i,(bh)_i. These are indexed inputs, not rotation classes, so no orbit-size or factor-N normalization occurs.
For any edge weights, define matrix entries as sums over all labeled edges with those endpoints. This retains parallel edges. Matrix rows are sources, columns are successors. Expansion of the trace of the ordered N-layer product sums precisely these closed walks. In particular define T(y) with edge weight y^e, and U(y) with edge weight (1+y)^{2−e}(1−y)^e. Then
W(y)=tr(T(y)^N)=Σ_{h∈S}y^{wt(ah)+wt(bh)},
E_B(y)=Σ_{z∈B_X}y^{wt z}=2^{−f}W(y).
The same correspondence applies to position-dependent weights, needed below.

4. Character orthogonality and logical subtraction.
For any binary linear subspace D, Σ_{q∈D}(−1)^{q·z} equals |D| when z∈D^⊥ and zero otherwise. In the latter case choose q_0 with q_0·z=1; translation by q_0 pairs terms of opposite sign. Summing this indicator against y^{wt z} and factoring over physical bits gives
E_{D^⊥}(y)=|D|^{−1}Σ_{q∈D}∏_j(1+(−1)^{q_j}y).
Apply this with D=B_Z=JB_X. Parameterizing q=JL(h) repeats each q exactly 2^f times. Since |D|=2^{N−f}, the resulting normalization is 2^{−N}. With uniform coordinate variables J only permutes factors, so the factor from layer i is (1+(−1)^αy)(1+(−1)^βy). Thus
E_C(y)=Σ_{z∈C_X}y^{wt z}=2^{−N}tr(U(y)^N).
It follows that
Q(y)=2^{−N}tr(U(y)^N)−2^{−f}tr(T(y)^N)=Σ_{z∈C_X\B_X}y^{wt z}.
Both divisions are exact coefficientwise, and Q has nonnegative integer coefficients with Q(0)=0. Its total count is Q(1)=2^{N+f}−2^{N−f}. If f=0, the inclusion B_X⊆C_X and equal dimensions imply Q=0, so distance is not applicable. If f>0, the first positive coefficient occurs at d_X. The permutation J proves d_Z=d_X. A nontrivial CSS logical Pauli has a nonboundary X or Z component whose support is contained in its Pauli support; a pure logical attains the smaller type distance. Hence the extracted value is the quantum distance.

5. Orientation-correct coordinate restrictions.
For every physical coordinate q choose an allowed set A_q equal to {0,1}, {0}, or {1}. Define integer polynomials
b_q(s)=1_{s∈A_q}y^s,
c_q(s)=Σ_{z∈A_q}(−1)^{sz}y^z.
At layer i, assign boundary edge weight b_{L,i}(α)b_{R,i}(β), and character edge weight c_{R,−i}(α)c_{L,−i}(β). Denote the summed-edge matrices by T_i^P,U_i^P. Then the restricted enumerators are
B_P(y)=2^{−f}tr(T_0^P⋯T_{N−1}^P),
C_P(y)=2^{−N}tr(U_0^P⋯U_{N−1}^P).
For boundaries, all preimages of the same vector have identical pin acceptance and weight, proving the first identity. For cycles, restrict each physical bit in the character-orthogonality calculation to A_q. The local factor becomes c_q((JL(h))_q). The output α at layer i occupies coordinate (R,−i) under J, and β occupies (L,−i); these are exactly the stated factors. Thus the second identity follows without assuming permutation symmetry of the pins. Consequently Q_P=C_P−B_P counts precisely pinned vectors in C_X\B_X, retaining their full physical weights, including pinned ones. All normalizations remain exact and Q_P has nonnegative integer coefficients.

6. Explicit coefficient algorithm.
Compute F by ordinary binary polynomial Euclid. Put s=2^R and precompute transitions and output bits. To evaluate any trace above, process each initial memory state a separately. Initialize V_0(a)=1 and every other state polynomial to zero. At layer i clear the next layer and for every state m and appended bit t perform
V_{i+1}(σ(m,t)) += V_i(m)g_i(m,t;y),
where g_i is the chosen edge polynomial. After N steps add V_N(a) to a trace accumulator. Iterate initial states and memories lexicographically and appended bits in order 0,1. This recurrence is matrix multiplication expanded by labeled edges and therefore automatically sums parallel edges. Store integer coefficients through degree 2i at layer i, or use arrays through degree 2N. Every edge polynomial has degree at most two, so no omitted coefficient can affect an answer. Normalize the two traces by their proved powers of two, subtract, and scan Q for its first positive coefficient when f>0.

7. Witness construction.
After finding d, begin with all coordinates free. Visit (L,0),…,(L,N−1),(R,0),…,(R,N−1). Tentatively pin the next coordinate to zero and evaluate [y^d]Q_P by the same recurrence. Keep zero if the count is positive; otherwise pin it to one. The two branches partition the previous set of weight-d nonboundary completions. That count starts positive and stays positive by induction. At the end the pins specify exactly one vector, so positivity proves that vector has weight d and belongs to C_X\B_X. Apply J for a minimum Z witness. There is at most one additional completion query per coordinate, with no enumeration of physical vectors hidden in the procedure.

8. Arithmetic model and resource bounds.
Use an indexed-array RAM, charging bit work for integer arithmetic and address manipulation; this is not a unit-cost arbitrary-integer or sequential-tape complexity claim. There are s initial states, N layers, at most 2s labeled edges per layer, and O(N) coefficients per polynomial. Every edge polynomial has degree at most two and coefficients of absolute value at most two. One trace therefore costs O(N²s²) coefficient operations, each a constant number of additions, subtractions, shifts, and small scalar multiplications.
For pinned and unpinned character weights the coefficient ℓ1 norm of an edge polynomial is at most four; boundary weights satisfy this bound too. From one initial state there are at most 2^i paths at depth i. The sum of absolute path-coefficient contributions is therefore at most 8^i. This also bounds partial accumulations before cancellation. Summing contributions from all initial states gives at most s8^N. Since R<N, all intermediate signed integers require O(N) bits, including a constant number of guard bits. Thus each coefficient operation costs O(N) bit work. Addresses require O(R+log(N+2)) bits, also absorbed in this bound. A trace query costs O(N³4^R) bit work. Naive polynomial gcd computation has a conservative O(N³) bit bound, and transition preprocessing costs O((R+1)2^R); both are absorbed.
Process initial states sequentially. Two layers, each with s polynomials of O(N) coefficients and O(N) bits per coefficient, use O(N²2^R) working bits. Accumulators, final enumerators, transition data and pins fit that bound. Exact division by 2^f and 2^N is coefficientwise signed binary division with zero remainder, justified by the counting identities; normalization and output scans cost O(N²) bit work. A constant number of traces computes distance. At most 2N additional paired traces construct a witness, giving O(N³4^R) coefficient operations and O(N⁴4^R) bit work with reusable O(N²2^R) storage. These bounds are polynomial in N for fixed span and exponential in span. They provide no practical performance comparison or efficient arbitrary-span algorithm.

9. Edge cases and falsifiers.
For R=0, anchoring gives a=b=1 and f=0. The single-state matrices, with both loops summed, are T=1+y² and U=(1+y)²+(1−y)²=2(1+y²). Hence E_C=E_B=(1+y²)^N and Q=0. The connected declared family permits this presentation only at N=1, although the algebraic identity holds for every N.
Generally W(1)=2^N by the indexed-input bijection. At y=1, only the 2^f inputs with L(h)=0 survive the U trace, each contributing 2^{2N}, proving E_C(1)=2^{N+f}. At y=0 the boundary trace counts the 2^f kernel inputs and the character trace counts all 2^N inputs, so both normalized constant coefficients are one. Restricted counts satisfy Q_P=Q_{P,q=0}+Q_{P,q=1} at every free coordinate.
Concrete falsifiers are failure of the indexed closed-walk bijection, a boundary fiber of size other than 2^f, an incorrect swapped/inverted pin location, nonintegral normalized coefficients, a negative Q_P coefficient, incorrect total counts, nonzero Q at f=0, or a returned witness with nonzero syndrome, boundary membership, or weight different from d. These are symbolic consistency targets; no executed validation is claimed.

10. Recipe group and scope.
The exact group remains independent support translations, a common unit multiplier modulo N, and block exchange. For a'=x^ra,b'=x^sb, the physical isometry P(u,v)=(x^ru,x^sv) maps boundaries to boundaries, while b'u'+a'v'=x^{r+s}(bu+av), so it also maps cycles to cycles. A common unit multiplier is the coefficient permutation induced by x^i↦x^{ui}; block exchange swaps the two physical blocks. Both preserve the cycle/boundary pair and weight. No module shear or additional equivalence is imposed. Span R and algorithmic cost belong to the chosen anchored presentation and need not be invariant under the group. Recipe classes are not identified with inequivalent quantum codes.
Every step applies to each allowed input N>R independently, including the entire pre-stabilization region and repeated-factor orders. There is no uncovered order region inside the stated claim. Fresh reviews of this unchanged integrated output, implementation certification, practical acceleration, compact predictors, M7 and formal completion remain outside this symbolic theorem.
claim: All-order exact distance reduction with constructive witnesses. Let a,b∈GF(2)[x] have constant coefficient 1, equal positive support weight, R=max(deg a,deg b)<N, and gcd(N,supp(a),supp(b))=1. Use H_X=[A|B], H_Z=[Bᵀ|Aᵀ], where row i of A is supported at i+supp(a), and similarly for B. Let F=gcd(a,b,x^N+1), with full multiplicities, and f=deg F. The transfer formulas below compute the ordinary Hamming-weight enumerator of physical X cycles outside X stabilizers, for every allowed N>R, including even orders and supports varying between inputs. For f>0 they give d_X=d_Z=d and reconstruct a minimum logical witness; for f=0 they report no logical distance. Distance costs O(N²4^R) integer coefficient operations, O(N³4^R) bit work, and O(N²2^R) working bits in the specified indexed-array model. Witness reconstruction costs O(N⁴4^R) bit work with the same storage. This establishes the symbolic exact-reduction route in the declared domain. Practical acceleration, efficient arbitrary-span computation, fresh dual review, M7, and Lean certification are not established.
